requirementSpec.intent: Build a polished Roblox main menu titled AURORA with Play, Settings, and Credits. Settings opens a panel containing a Music on/off toggle and Volume slider. Credits opens a small panel. Both panels require Close controls. Play must close the menu and fire a clearly named local hook for game integration. Presentation should use rich glossy cyan/cobalt artwork with thick navy edges, warm gold highlights, ornamental corner details, and a title plate, while keeping text live and readable. Use Gemini-generated matching skins and icons where appropriate, with native Roblox layout for the background and restrained decoration. Support desktop and mobile only. Create only the requested features and exclude unrelated game systems.

designPlan.artDirection: A premium fantasy-tech menu built around a glossy cyan-to-cobalt material system with thick navy framing and restrained warm-gold highlights. The composition centers a large ornamental title plate for the live AURORA wordmark, then stacks three main actions beneath it with Play clearly dominant in scale, glow, and spacing. Decorative energy is concentrated at the four corners and title area only, leaving the background largely native and calm so interactive elements remain the focus. Panels use the same shared glossy skin and navy edging as the buttons, with gold accent lines reserved for selected edges, title trims, and active control states. Text remains live, high-contrast, and minimally outlined for readability against rich surfaces. Matching Gemini-generated assets are planned only for button skins, panel skin, title plate, ornamental corner details, and the icon family; slider and toggle behavior layers remain native Roblox controls styled with gradients, strokes, and gold active fills to preserve responsiveness and state clarity.

composition.focalPoint: The focal point is the vertical center-top title plate carrying the live AURORA title, immediately followed by an unmistakably larger Play button. Settings and Credits form a coherent secondary action stack directly under Play, while contextual panels appear centered above the menu stack without displacing the primary title hierarchy.
secondaryRegions: background_frame provides a restrained full-screen stage with subtle native gradients and dark vignette balance.
corner_ornaments frame the composition at the safe-area corners without creating extra navigation.
settings_modal appears centered as a medium panel overlay with close control at top-right and two clean content rows.
credits_modal appears centered as a smaller panel overlay with title, body text, and close control.
composition.alignmentSystem: Use a strong centered vertical axis for title and main actions. Modal overlays are also center-anchored to preserve compositional stability. Within panels, rows align left for labels and right for controls, with close buttons pinned top-right inside panel padding. Desktop uses a centered column with generous breathing room; mobile compresses into a tighter center column while maintaining clear separation between title, actions, and modal content.

visualSystem.colorRationale: Cyan and cobalt carry the glossy premium identity across all primary surfaces, while deep navy provides structural edge weight and readable containment. Warm gold is deliberately sparse so highlights feel luxurious rather than noisy, reserved for title trim, active states, and subtle specular accents. Neutral dark blues suppress the background and keep the menu readable on both desktop and mobile. Success and danger exist for control state support but are used minimally.
visualSystem.outlineStyle: Thick navy outer framing with lighter inner cyan stroke accents on major skins. Interactive controls use 2-4px equivalent stroke hierarchy through UIStroke; text is not heavily outlined except very light shadow or subtle dark backing on display elements.
visualSystem.shadowStyle: Soft layered shadows with short-range dark navy contact shadow and a restrained cyan bloom on the primary CTA only. Panels receive deeper ambient shadow than buttons to clearly float above the background without overwhelming the screen.

display.treatment: Used only for the live AURORA title. Tight tracking, bright white-cyan fill, minimal dark shadow, no heavy outline. Centered within the title plate.

heading.treatment: Used for panel titles and important section labels. Crisp white with subtle gold accent support nearby, not on the glyphs.

button.treatment: High legibility uppercase or title case with centered alignment. White text with slight dark shadow for contrast over glossy skins.

body.treatment: Readable live text for credits body and row labels with generous line height and soft blue-white tone.

caption.treatment: Used for auxiliary values like the volume percentage, with subdued but still clear contrast.

numeric.treatment: Reserved for live volume value display if shown, with tabular-feeling spacing and bright contrast.

badge.treatment: Not emphasized in this menu, but kept consistent for any small pill-like labels if needed inside panels.

motionSystem.hover: Interactive buttons and pointer-relevant controls receive a restrained lift, gloss travel, and rim brightening. The Play button gets the strongest hover emphasis, while secondary buttons and close buttons use smaller amplitude. Panels themselves do not hover; only their actionable controls do.
motionSystem.press: All actionable controls use a quick compress-and-settle response. Buttons scale down slightly and shift inward; toggle and slider handles compress subtly during manipulation. Motion should feel premium and controlled, never bouncy or cartoonish.
motionSystem.entrance: On initial menu reveal, title plate and action dock fade and rise in together with short stagger: title first, then Play, then Settings and Credits. Modal panels fade and scale from 0.96 to 1.0 when opened, with background remaining stable.
motionSystem.release: Controls spring back softly to default state after press release, and modal closes fade quickly with a slight scale-down to 0.98 before hiding. Release motion remains shorter than entrance to keep the interface snappy.
motionSystem.reducedMotion: Disable lift offsets and stagger; keep only short opacity changes and minimal scale differences. Slider and toggle still update state immediately but without extra animated flourish.
motionSystem.touchBehavior: Touch devices use Activated and direct drag interactions only. No synthesized hover animations; instead, show immediate press-state darkening/compression on touch-down and restore on release.

audioSystem.touchBehavior: No UI sounds on touch or desktop because sounds were not requested.
audioSystem.fallbackBehavior: If a project later enables UI sounds, use a quiet premium hover/click family with the same debounce contract; otherwise remain silent and report sounds as intentionally omitted.

responsiveStrategy.desktop: Build _NexusDesktop with a centered column composition: ornamental title plate, dominant Play CTA, then Settings and Credits. Settings and Credits modals are centered overlays with ample whitespace and moderate panel widths. Desktop retains richer gloss, stronger shadows, and slightly more ornament presence.
responsiveStrategy.mobile: Build _NexusMobile independently rather than scaling desktop. Keep the same semantic node names under the mobile group, but widen the action stack, reduce ornament intensity, tighten vertical spacing, enlarge touch areas, and widen modals. Preserve the title-first then Play-first hierarchy. Touch targets for all actionable controls stay at or above 48px, and hover-specific behavior is removed.
responsiveStrategy.tablet: Tablet uses the desktop group because only desktop and mobile were requested as supported targets. The layout should still interpolate safely between phone and desktop sizes via constraints, but no tablet-specific visual branch is declared beyond the required breakpoint metadata.

implementationNotes: Create both _NexusDesktop and _NexusMobile Frame groups at View.build() return, with desktop visible initially and runtime switching to mobile when min(viewport.X, viewport.Y) < 600.

Keep exact nodeName values from the library template for all supported nodes included here: BackgroundLayer, BackgroundRoot, BackgroundOrnaments, MainMenuDock, TitlePlate, AuroraTitle, PlayButton, SettingsButton, CreditsButton, SettingsModal, SettingsTitle, SettingsCloseButton, MusicRow, MusicLabel, MusicToggle, VolumeRow, VolumeLabel, VolumeSlider, VolumeValue, CreditsModal, CreditsTitle, CreditsBody, CreditsCloseButton, OnPlayRequestedHook, PanelControllerBehavior.
Do not add unsupported navigation or feature panels. Omit SettingsSeparator because it is unnecessary.
Use one shared generated skin for SettingsButton and CreditsButton, one shared generated skin for both close buttons, and one shared generated panel skin for SettingsModal and CreditsModal.
Keep title, button labels, settings labels, and credits text as live Roblox TextLabel/TextButton text; do not bake lettering into generated art.

Despite the original artwork request mentioning slider and toggle skins, follow the authoritative library policy: MusicToggle and VolumeSlider remain native Roblox controls built from Frames, UICorner, UIStroke, and UIGradient, styled to match the theme.
Use generated icon family for PlayButton, SettingsButton, CreditsButton, and both close buttons; icons must be distinct but visually coherent.
Implement Play so it closes the menu root and then fires the clearly named local hook represented by OnPlayRequestedHook using a local callback or Bindable-style contract within the client UI layer.
PanelControllerBehavior should handle opening SettingsModal, opening CreditsModal, closing either panel, and ensuring only one modal is visible at a time.

Main menu actions should remain accessible when no modal is open; when a modal opens, keep focus visually on the modal via elevated shadow and slightly dimmed hero menu if desired using native transparency changes only.
Use local helper functions in View for repeated skin assembly and text style application. Put reusable interaction tweens in a shared ButtonEffects module rather than duplicating code per button.
No audio assets should be fabricated. Keep the UI silent because sounds were not requested.
All actionable controls must use Activated-compatible wiring for touch and pointer support. Touch should never rely on MouseEnter/MouseLeave behavior.
Use UITextSizeConstraint for title, button text, headings, and body text so desktop and mobile remain readable without manual per-device text objects.
Generated artwork requests should preserve aspect ratio and baked palette; native gradients and strokes should echo the same cyan/cobalt/navy/gold logic for cohesion.
Background decoration must remain restrained and must not imply additional systems, progression, or world map content.

designPlan.artDirection: A premium fantasy-tech menu built around a glossy cyan-to-cobalt material system with thick navy framing and restrained warm-gold highlights. The composition centers a large ornamental title plate for the live AURORA wordmark, then stacks three main actions beneath it with Play clearly dominant in scale, glow, and spacing. Decorative energy is concentrated at the four corners and title area only, leaving the background largely native and calm so interactive elements remain the focus. Panels use the same shared glossy skin and navy edging as the buttons, with gold accent lines reserved for selected edges, title trims, and active control states. Text remains live, high-contrast, and minimally outlined for readability against rich surfaces. Matching Gemini-generated assets are planned only for button skins, panel skin, title plate, ornamental corner details, and the icon family; slider and toggle behavior layers remain native Roblox controls styled with gradients, strokes, and gold active fills to preserve responsiveness and state clarity.

composition.focalPoint: The focal point is the vertical center-top title plate carrying the live AURORA title, immediately followed by an unmistakably larger Play button. Settings and Credits form a coherent secondary action stack directly under Play, while contextual panels appear centered above the menu stack without displacing the primary title hierarchy.
secondaryRegions: background_frame provides a restrained full-screen stage with subtle native gradients and dark vignette balance.
corner_ornaments frame the composition at the safe-area corners without creating extra navigation.
settings_modal appears centered as a medium panel overlay with close control at top-right and two clean content rows.
credits_modal appears centered as a smaller panel overlay with title, body text, and close control.
composition.alignmentSystem: Use a strong centered vertical axis for title and main actions. Modal overlays are also center-anchored to preserve compositional stability. Within panels, rows align left for labels and right for controls, with close buttons pinned top-right inside panel padding. Desktop uses a centered column with generous breathing room; mobile compresses into a tighter center column while maintaining clear separation between title, actions, and modal content.

visualSystem.colorRationale: Cyan and cobalt carry the glossy premium identity across all primary surfaces, while deep navy provides structural edge weight and readable containment. Warm gold is deliberately sparse so highlights feel luxurious rather than noisy, reserved for title trim, active states, and subtle specular accents. Neutral dark blues suppress the background and keep the menu readable on both desktop and mobile. Success and danger exist for control state support but are used minimally.
visualSystem.outlineStyle: Thick navy outer framing with lighter inner cyan stroke accents on major skins. Interactive controls use 2-4px equivalent stroke hierarchy through UIStroke; text is not heavily outlined except very light shadow or subtle dark backing on display elements.
visualSystem.shadowStyle: Soft layered shadows with short-range dark navy contact shadow and a restrained cyan bloom on the primary CTA only. Panels receive deeper ambient shadow than buttons to clearly float above the background without overwhelming the screen.

display.treatment: Used only for the live AURORA title. Tight tracking, bright white-cyan fill, minimal dark shadow, no heavy outline. Centered within the title plate.

heading.treatment: Used for panel titles and important section labels. Crisp white with subtle gold accent support nearby, not on the glyphs.

button.treatment: High legibility uppercase or title case with centered alignment. White text with slight dark shadow for contrast over glossy skins.

body.treatment: Readable live text for credits body and row labels with generous line height and soft blue-white tone.

caption.treatment: Used for auxiliary values like the volume percentage, with subdued but still clear contrast.

numeric.treatment: Reserved for live volume value display if shown, with tabular-feeling spacing and bright contrast.

badge.treatment: Not emphasized in this menu, but kept consistent for any small pill-like labels if needed inside panels.

motionSystem.hover: Interactive buttons and pointer-relevant controls receive a restrained lift, gloss travel, and rim brightening. The Play button gets the strongest hover emphasis, while secondary buttons and close buttons use smaller amplitude. Panels themselves do not hover; only their actionable controls do.
motionSystem.press: All actionable controls use a quick compress-and-settle response. Buttons scale down slightly and shift inward; toggle and slider handles compress subtly during manipulation. Motion should feel premium and controlled, never bouncy or cartoonish.
motionSystem.entrance: On initial menu reveal, title plate and action dock fade and rise in together with short stagger: title first, then Play, then Settings and Credits. Modal panels fade and scale from 0.96 to 1.0 when opened, with background remaining stable.
motionSystem.release: Controls spring back softly to default state after press release, and modal closes fade quickly with a slight scale-down to 0.98 before hiding. Release motion remains shorter than entrance to keep the interface snappy.
motionSystem.reducedMotion: Disable lift offsets and stagger; keep only short opacity changes and minimal scale differences. Slider and toggle still update state immediately but without extra animated flourish.
motionSystem.touchBehavior: Touch devices use Activated and direct drag interactions only. No synthesized hover animations; instead, show immediate press-state darkening/compression on touch-down and restore on release.

audioSystem.touchBehavior: No UI sounds on touch or desktop because sounds were not requested.
audioSystem.fallbackBehavior: If a project later enables UI sounds, use a quiet premium hover/click family with the same debounce contract; otherwise remain silent and report sounds as intentionally omitted.

responsiveStrategy.desktop: Build _NexusDesktop with a centered column composition: ornamental title plate, dominant Play CTA, then Settings and Credits. Settings and Credits modals are centered overlays with ample whitespace and moderate panel widths. Desktop retains richer gloss, stronger shadows, and slightly more ornament presence.
responsiveStrategy.mobile: Build _NexusMobile independently rather than scaling desktop. Keep the same semantic node names under the mobile group, but widen the action stack, reduce ornament intensity, tighten vertical spacing, enlarge touch areas, and widen modals. Preserve the title-first then Play-first hierarchy. Touch targets for all actionable controls stay at or above 48px, and hover-specific behavior is removed.
responsiveStrategy.tablet: Tablet uses the desktop group because only desktop and mobile were requested as supported targets. The layout should still interpolate safely between phone and desktop sizes via constraints, but no tablet-specific visual branch is declared beyond the required breakpoint metadata.

implementationNotes: Create both _NexusDesktop and _NexusMobile Frame groups at View.build() return, with desktop visible initially and runtime switching to mobile when min(viewport.X, viewport.Y) < 600.

Keep exact nodeName values from the library template for all supported nodes included here: BackgroundLayer, BackgroundRoot, BackgroundOrnaments, MainMenuDock, TitlePlate, AuroraTitle, PlayButton, SettingsButton, CreditsButton, SettingsModal, SettingsTitle, SettingsCloseButton, MusicRow, MusicLabel, MusicToggle, VolumeRow, VolumeLabel, VolumeSlider, VolumeValue, CreditsModal, CreditsTitle, CreditsBody, CreditsCloseButton, OnPlayRequestedHook, PanelControllerBehavior.
Do not add unsupported navigation or feature panels. Omit SettingsSeparator because it is unnecessary.
Use one shared generated skin for SettingsButton and CreditsButton, one shared generated skin for both close buttons, and one shared generated panel skin for SettingsModal and CreditsModal.
Keep title, button labels, settings labels, and credits text as live Roblox TextLabel/TextButton text; do not bake lettering into generated art.

Despite the original artwork request mentioning slider and toggle skins, follow the authoritative library policy: MusicToggle and VolumeSlider remain native Roblox controls built from Frames, UICorner, UIStroke, and UIGradient, styled to match the theme.
Use generated icon family for PlayButton, SettingsButton, CreditsButton, and both close buttons; icons must be distinct but visually coherent.
Implement Play so it closes the menu root and then fires the clearly named local hook represented by OnPlayRequestedHook using a local callback or Bindable-style contract within the client UI layer.
PanelControllerBehavior should handle opening SettingsModal, opening CreditsModal, closing either panel, and ensuring only one modal is visible at a time.

Main menu actions should remain accessible when no modal is open; when a modal opens, keep focus visually on the modal via elevated shadow and slightly dimmed hero menu if desired using native transparency changes only.
Use local helper functions in View for repeated skin assembly and text style application. Put reusable interaction tweens in a shared ButtonEffects module rather than duplicating code per button.
No audio assets should be fabricated. Keep the UI silent because sounds were not requested.
All actionable controls must use Activated-compatible wiring for touch and pointer support. Touch should never rely on MouseEnter/MouseLeave behavior.
Use UITextSizeConstraint for title, button text, headings, and body text so desktop and mobile remain readable without manual per-device text objects.
Generated artwork requests should preserve aspect ratio and baked palette; native gradients and strokes should echo the same cyan/cobalt/navy/gold logic for cohesion.
Background decoration must remain restrained and must not imply additional systems, progression, or world map content.
